cover.title: Infrastructure & Cloud Optimization
cover.subtitle: Five plays — FinOps, acquisition cleanup, MSP restructure, network rationalisation, storage hardening
cover.meta: Hypothesis H2 · {monthYear} · PwC Confidential · Subject to CIO validation
cover.hook: Five plays, not three. No data centers — but Culligan's acquisition-heavy model has left a long tail of duplicated infrastructure, fragmented identity, unmanaged circuits, and a $2.04M cloud run-rate (TBM Cloud Services pool) with negligible FinOps discipline. The prize is $1.7–3.5M — and it demands acquisition cleanup, commercially-structured MSP contracts, and hard FinOps discipline.
cover.source: Source: TBM Spend Baseline (7.10) · Cloud Billing Q1 2026 · Gartner IT Metrics 2024 · CrowdStrike 2024 Threat Report

executiveSummary.title: Executive summary
executiveSummary.sectionTitle: The problem is structural, the opportunity is real, and the clock is running

rows.finding: 19 BUs procure infrastructure independently — no group-level leverage or visibility. Group MSP estate carries zero contractual leverage; auto-escalation 3–7% p.a. Cloud Services run-rate $2.04M (TBM pool) with ~0% Reserved Instance coverage and negligible tagging. Ultrapure/WaterFlex (11 sites) migrating to NetSuite on Azure independently — shadow CapEx. 137 AMER FortiGates on firmware associated with critical CVEs — live ransomware exposure.

Acquisition-driven growth compounds fragmentation with every deal — each adds identity forests, MSP contracts, backup tools and Azure subscriptions never rationalised on close. 83% of IT spend locked in auto-renewing contracts — inaction guarantees 3–7% annual cost increase. Culligan's $3.4B revenue scale gives material vendor leverage it is currently not using at any level.

Infrastructure towers (Compute+Storage+Network) = 15% of total IT spend ($13.0M of $87.2M per TBM baseline); Network is the largest single tower at $10.05M. Infrastructure & Cloud is the category with the most fragmentation-driven cost growth and least group oversight. Each year without intervention: 3–7% auto-escalation on renewing contracts + cloud sprawl (+9%/qtr unmanaged).

$1.7–3.5M net annual savings (H2 total, Year 3). Year 1 quick wins (FinOps alone): $0.4–0.8M. Five sequenced plays over 0–36 months. Gross savings $2.0–4.4M before investment. Plays 3–4 (MSP, circuits) are H4-mandate gated; H4 owns the full cross-BU MSP commercial renegotiation ($3.1–4.0M).

01. Formalize FinOps immediately — rightsize, enforce tagging, commit stable prod to Reserved Instances (Play 1, 0–12m). 02. Treat acquisition infrastructure debt as the primary structural lever: consolidate identity forests, rationalize backup, decommission inherited subscriptions (Play 2, 6–18m). 03. Restructure the MSP commercially — committed 5–10%/yr price reduction, gain-share, and automation milestone triggers (Play 3, 6–24m). 04. Remediate 137 critically-vulnerable FortiGates on a security timeline (Play 4 prerequisite). 05. Commission circuit & carrier inventory across all sites before claiming a savings ceiling (Play 4, 12–36m).

NOW (0–12m): $0.4–0.8M — FinOps, tagging, RI commitments, acquisition inventory, FortiGate remediation, MSP RFP. NEXT (6–24m): $0.8–1.9M — identity consolidation, backup rationalisation, MSP contract, Tier-0 automation. LATER (12–36m): $0.3–0.8M — circuit inventory & RFP, storage tiering, DR consolidation, platform hire.

benchmarks.title: Benchmarking — spend vs. peers and operating maturity
benchmarks.healthWarning: In acquisition-heavy companies, spending below peers can signal underinvestment, deferred tech debt, or a cost base that hasn't yet absorbed the acquired entities' run-rate. Directional context only — not evidence of efficiency.

spendMetrics.implication: Compute+Storage+Network per TBM baseline on $87.2M visible spend.
Q1 Azure billing extract shows larger gross estate (~$3.6–4.0M); lenses differ intentionally.
$0.9–1.4M p.a. opportunity if confirmed zero RI on stable prod.
~30% (~$0.6M/yr of TBM pool) unmapped — FinOps prerequisite.
21% of cloud spend is non-prod (~$0.77M/yr annualised from Q1 2026).
31,000+ JML requests; sequential multi-team manual process.
Without gain-share in contract, MSP captures automation benefit.
137 devices on critical CVE firmware — CrowdStrike #1 ransomware vector in industrial sector.

impactRisks.title: Security exposure
impactRisks.finding: 137 FortiGates (30% of AMER fleet) on firmware associated with critical CVEs. Spend on network hardware is below peer range — signs of deferred refresh, not lean design.
impactRisks.action: Remediate the 137 devices on a security timeline. Cost: ~$480K one-time (137 × $3,500 licensing). Non-negotiable.

impactRisks.title: Governance gap
impactRisks.finding: ~$1.1M/yr of cloud spend sits in unmapped subscriptions with no BU owner. Virtual Agent deflection 1.1% vs. 15–20% industry target. RI coverage ~0% on stable production.
impactRisks.action: FinOps is not optional. Enforce tagging, commit stable workloads to RIs, schedule off-hours shutdown for non-production. Self-funding within 12 months.

impactRisks.title: Hidden cost base
impactRisks.finding: Rubrik, Nasuni, and Azure-native backup run in parallel. Multiple AD forests live. ~30% of Azure subscriptions unmapped, many inherited from acquisitions.
impactRisks.action: Commission an acquisition infrastructure inventory before the next annual budget cycle. Without it, the savings case remains directional.

plays.title: The five plays
plays.lead: Expanded from three to capture acquisition cleanup and a commercially-structured MSP. Savings ranges designed to be non-overlapping — backup rationalisation in Play 2 only; Azure cleanup split Play 1 (organic) / Play 2 (acquired).

items.name: Optimize — Azure FinOps
items.focus: Rightsizing · RIs · Off-hours scheduling · Tagging enforcement · Automated parking · Orphaned VM reclaim · Inherited subscription cleanup

items.name: Cleanup — Acquisition Infrastructure
items.focus: Identity consolidation (AD/Entra ID) · Backup rationalisation (Rubrik + Nasuni + Azure-native) · Inherited Azure subscriptions · Duplicate NOC/monitoring · DR deduplication

items.name: Automate — MSP + Service Model
items.focus: Committed 5–10%/yr price reduction · Gain-share · Unit-rate compression · Tier-0 self-heal · JML automation. Infra MSP sub-component only — H4 owns full MSP renegotiation ($3.1–4.0M).

items.name: See-then-cut — Network · Circuits · Firewall
items.focus: Circuit inventory build (all carriers, all sites) · Carrier consolidation · FortiGate firmware remediation · Firewall ops into MSP. No circuit visibility — savings ceiling cannot be stated until inventory is built.

items.name: Harden — Storage · Backup · Platform
items.focus: Storage tiering (Cool/Archive) · Redundant DR copy removal · Retention policy · Distributed-cloud platform owner (Head of Platform hire). Sequence behind Play 2 backup rationalisation.

maIntegrationPipeline.title: Active integration backlog — Americas (July 2026)
maIntegrationPipeline.lead: The M&A integration opportunity is not a large legacy backlog. The active pipeline covers 19 users and 2 sites (plus 1 upcoming deal). Culligan has standardised locations on CommandLink at $230/month — not the $850/month DIA assumed in prior models. Identity is consolidated. The savings lever is integration process efficiency and the Ultrapure anomaly.

rows.items: Phone number + email domain transfer only
1 site still on legacy ISP; migrate to CommandLink on expiry
FortiGate 60F, M365 migration, backup, security stack
Pre-close — scope TBC; assume similar to 7/1 profile
Legacy WaterFlex ERP on Azure VMs — heading to NetSuite, NOT IFS; running independently from Culligan IT

implications: Circuit rationalisation is largely done — active pipeline locations confirmed on CommandLink at $230/mo. Scott Sier to confirm whether legacy acquired sites remain on higher-cost DIA circuits.
Ultrapure/WaterFlex needs a decision — 11 sites on Azure-hosted WaterFlex heading to NetSuite. Recommended: bring under Group IT governance or formally assign BU cost accountability to GM.
The opportunity is per-deal efficiency — rapid, standardised integration onto FortiGate, CommandLink, M365, and the security stack within a defined SLA.
maIntegrationPipeline.source: Mike Baerson (IT M&A Lead, Americas), July 2026. Pipeline covers Americas only.

roadmap.title: Sequenced roadmap
roadmap.lead: Start FinOps now; add acquisition cleanup and the MSP; gate circuits on inventory. Critical dependency: dedicated programme resource required to execute Plays 1–3 in parallel.

actions: Stand up FinOps: rightsize, schedule off-hours, reclaim orphaned VM disks — Play 1
Enforce tagging standard — every subscription mapped to a BU — Play 1
Commit stable prod base to Reserved Instances / Savings Plans — Play 1
Remediate 137 critically-vulnerable FortiGates with SecOps — Play 4
Structure MSP RFP with committed price-reduction clauses (5–10%/yr), gain-share, automation triggers — Play 3
Consolidate identity: merge AD forests → single Entra ID — Play 2
Rationalise backup: consolidate Rubrik + Nasuni + Azure-native — Plays 2 & 5
Decommission inherited Azure subscriptions and DR environments — Play 2
Award MSP contract; deploy Tier-0 self-heal and JML automation — Play 3
Build circuit inventory (all carriers, all sites); commission carrier consolidation RFP — Play 4
Distributed-cloud platform owner (Head of Platform hire)

bottomLine.title: Five plays, not three — and the root cause is now the lead play
stats: Cleanup: acquisition debt is the root cause
Automate: MSP only saves if contract is structured commercially
Inventory then cut: build circuit inventory before claiming ceiling
bottomLine.saving: $1.7–3.5M net annually — by treating acquisition debt as the root cause, not a footnote
bottomLine.nextStep: Spending less than peers may reflect technical debt and underinvestment, not efficiency. Fix the FortiGate vulnerability now regardless of the broader roadmap.
